title: Microsoft Viva: identifiable export of Copilot metrics from the Copilot Dashboard
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, identification access policy, export prerequisites and PowerShell calls remain supported by Microsoft's current documentation. Minor corrections should complete the admin navigation paths and align the governance checklist with the controls table.

claims.claim: The planned feature exports identifiable row-level Copilot Dashboard metrics for reporting and deeper analysis.
claims.quote: This enables users to export Identifiable row-level Copilot metrics from the Copilot Dashboard for reporting and deeper analysis.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Identification reveals named employees rather than just anonymised metrics.
claims.quote: Identification is the set of capabilities that lets your organization move from anonymized metrics to known users - surfacing named employees (identified outputs) when added precision is needed and permitted.

claims.claim: Week-level export contains the past six months of metrics.
claims.quote: You can download week-level metrics spanning the past six months, or day-level metrics spanning the past 28 days.

claims.claim: Day-level export contains the past 28 days of metrics.
claims.quote: You can download week-level metrics spanning the past six months, or day-level metrics spanning the past 28 days.

claims.claim: Eligible users select Export data in the Copilot Dashboard, then Export by week or Export by day.
claims.quote: Eligible tenants and users can export directly from the Copilot Dashboard by selecting Export data. ... Select Export by week, to download the last six months of data; or select Export by day, to download the last 28 days of data.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Export replaces personal identifiers with anonymised IDs unless an administrator enables identifiable export for the exporting user, when identifiable fields are also included.
claims.quote: Personal identifiers are removed and replaced with anonymized IDs, unless your administrator has enabled identifiable export for you. If your administrator has enabled identifiable export, the export also includes identifiable fields.

claims.quote: Copilot Dashboard data export (Private Preview)

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact

claims.claim: A dedicated VFAM policy governs access to identification and identified outputs.
claims.quote: Access is governed by a dedicated Viva Feature Access Management (VFAM) policy, so administrators decide exactly who in the organization can identify users and view identified outputs.

claims.claim: Users cannot customise the exports, so they receive the metrics included in the selected export type.
claims.quote: Each week-level export contains six months of week-level aggregated Copilot metrics at the user level (with identifiers removed) across the adoption and impact pages. Each day-level export contains 28 days of aggregated metrics with removed identifiers. You can't customize the exports.

claims.claim: Microsoft calls identification sensitive because identified outputs reveal named users.
claims.quote: Because identified outputs reveal named users, identification is a sensitive capability.

claims.claim: Identification access can be enabled through Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app and feature > Access setting > On.
claims.quote: From the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Viva from the settings menu. Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. Select Create a policy. ... Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off to enable or disable the feature.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].ui.path and its rendered table path to 'Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app and feature > Access setting > On'. The existing steps are supported; the initial settings heading is omitted.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId <featureId> -Name <policyName> -IsFeatureEnabled $true -Everyone enables the selected identification feature tenant-wide.
claims.quote: The IsFeatureEnabled parameter specifies whether or not the feature is enabled by the policy. Valid values are: $true: The feature is enabled by the policy. $false: The feature is not enabled by the policy.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchange/add-vivamodulefeaturepolicy?view=exchange-ps to sources to cite the reference that explicitly documents the printed command's parameters and $true value. The call itself needs no change.

claims.claim: The existing export policy can be disabled through Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app and feature > Access setting > Off.
claims.quote: From the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Viva from the settings menu. Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. Select Create a policy. ... Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off to enable or disable the feature.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].ui.path and its rendered table path to 'Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app and feature > Access setting > Off'. The existing steps are supported; the initial settings heading is omitted.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId <featureId> -Name <policyName> -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone disables the selected export feature tenant-wide, subject to its documented role exception.
claims.quote: Now that you have the featureID, use the Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy PowerShell cmdlet to create an access policy for the feature. ... If you want to disable the feature for all users, use the -Everyone parameter instead.

claims.claim: Replacing -Everyone with -GroupIds or -UserIds scopes an identification pilot to groups or individual users.
claims.quote: The policy disables the feature for the specified users and group members. If you want to disable the feature for all users, use the -Everyone parameter instead.
